claim: Work is completed by the sixth day; the seventh is distinguished by cessation/rest.
After two days: revival; on the third day: raising/living.
Six is treated as a perfect/order number rather than a literal duration; time is indexed by heavenly motion; seven is assigned a distinct post-six role.
Solar deity withdraws into a cave and later emerges, restoring light.

source: Watamashi narrative reported in Saida Khalmirzaeva, Rites of Blind Biwa Players
claim: A later ritual narrative contains three days and three nights of mikagura before the cave remains closed; subsequent musical/interpersonal action precedes emergence.

source: ETCSL c.1.4.1, Inana's descent to the nether world, lines 164-281
claim: Inana is made a corpse and hung on a hook; after three days and three nights Ninshubur begins the rescue procedure; Enki later supplies life-giving plant and water, after which Inana arises.
does_not_establish: resurrection occurred exactly at the end of the third day

claim: Inana passes seven gates; at the sixth her measuring rod and line are removed, at the seventh her final garment is removed; immediately afterward she is judged and becomes a corpse.

source: Epic of Gilgamesh Tablet XI, flood account, ETANA translation lines ~127-132
claim: The flood is described as raging for six days and seven nights; when the seventh day arrives, the gale relents and the deluge ends.

source: Vīdēvdād 19.27ff and later tradition as summarized by Encyclopaedia Iranica
claim: The soul remains near the corpse for three days/nights and at dawn after the third day proceeds toward the Činwad bridge and judgment.
Nachiketas remains three nights fasting in the house of Yama/Death; Yama then returns and grants three boons, one for each night.
does_not_establish: direct relation to Near Eastern traditions

source: Kojiki chapter 1, Kokugakuin University English translation
claim: At the beginning of heaven and earth, three solitary deities appear and hide their bodies; next, two further solitary deities appear and also hide their bodies.

source: Bundahišn creation accounts summarized in Encyclopaedia Iranica, Elements i
claim: The tradition preserves both a six-creation scheme associated with six gāhānbārs ending with man and seven-stage creation accounts that include fire (or, in another variant, Ohrmazd).
Humanity is created in Tablet VI, but the proclamation of Marduk's names already begins late in Tablet VI and continues through Tablet VII.
